internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all four morphological classes the root turns on one idea: lacking real substance so that a thing has no standing and comes to nothing. A deed can 'baTala' (become void, 7:118); God can 'abTala' magic, charity, or deeds (nullify them, 10:81/2:264/47:33); and 'al-baaTil' is the thing with no reality that vanishes when the real (al-Haqq) arrives — it is 'ever bound to vanish' (17:81), 'can neither originate nor restore' (34:49), is 'crushed' (21:18) and 'blotted out' (42:24). Decisively, 8:8 uses the root's own causative on its own noun — 'nullify the void' (yubTila l-baaTil) — bridging verb and substantive internally. Two peripheries strain the nucleus: the adverbial 'baaTilan' = 'in vain / to no end' (38:27, 3:191), a register shift that still bridges via 'no real purpose'; and, more seriously, the frozen juridical idiom 'akl al-amwaal bi-l-baaTil' = 'consuming wealth wrongfully' (2:188, 4:29, 4:161, 9:34), whose operative contrast is lawful/consensual acquisition, not truth or perishing — a resistant lexicalized sub-class that caps the grade.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: bTl does NOT entail: (1) moral sin (ithm) — 2:188 lists 'bi-l-baaTil' (invalid basis) and 'bi-l-ithm' (sinful means) as separate wrong modes in one verse; (2) a lie/false assertion (kadhib) — 42:24 separates 'iftaraa kadhiban' from 'al-baaTil', and the root also governs deeds, wealth, deities, and creation-purpose; (3) mere factual error — the entailment is ontological groundlessness / non-endurance (34:49, 17:81), not epistemic mistake; (4) weakness or smallness — al-baaTil can be loud and aggressive in disputation (18:56, 40:5) yet still void; (5) generic purposelessness — 'in vain' is licensed only in the accusative baaTilan (38:27, 3:191). Its voidness is intrinsic (kaana zahuuqan, 17:81; laa yubdiʾu wa-laa yuʿiid, 34:49): the crushing by al-Haqq exposes rather than constitutes it.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: In the juridical collocation akl al-amwaal bi-l-baaTil (2:188:5:3, 4:29:8:3, 4:161:9:3, 9:34:12:3) the operative contrast is lawful/consensual acquisition — 'illaa an takuwna tijaaratan ʿan taraaDin' (4:29) — not al-Haqq, nor perishing/non-endurance. The activated axis is legitimacy of title/entitlement; 2:188 routes the wrongful wealth 'ilaa l-Hukkaam' (a legal-procedural frame). The text condemns the taking as wrongful/without valid basis and never marks the wealth as void or as coming to nothing, so the root's distinctive 'perishes before the real' content is NOT demonstrated for this class; it fits only the thinnest 'lacking valid ground' abstraction. This is a coherent, frozen, four-occurrence lexicalized nominal sub-class.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses independently converge on MODERATE / REPRESENTATIVE. The nucleus 'void of real standing/valid foundation → null, non-enduring; the perishable counter-pole of al-Haqq' is broad (36 occ, 4 morphological classes), distinctive (systematic Haqq/baaTil polarity with vanishing/impotence collocations: zahuuq 17:81, yadmaghu 21:18, laa yubdiʾu 34:49, yamHu 42:24, jufaaʾ 13:17), and internally bridged by adversarially-clean linchpins (8:8 yubTila l-baaTila; 7:118 baTala after waqaʿa l-Haqq; 2:264/47:33 causative on GOOD deeds proving core = efficacy not truth-value).
